meta.title: Operation of Moisture Analyzer in Pharmacognosy Laboratory

sections.purpose: To rapidly determine the moisture content (loss on drying) of crude drug powders and herbal materials using a halogen or infrared moisture analyzer for pharmacopeial standardization.
sections.scope: Applicable to Pharmacognosy laboratory for quality control of crude drugs — moisture content is a mandatory IP/WHO parameter for drug standardization.
procedure: Switch on the moisture analyzer and allow it to warm up for at least 10 minutes.
Level the instrument using the built-in spirit level and adjusting feet.
Open the analyzer lid and clean the sample pan with a dry, lint-free cloth.
Tare the empty pan by pressing the 'Tare' button — display should show 0.00 g.
Set the drying temperature per pharmacopeial requirement: 100–105°C for most crude drugs; 60°C for volatile-containing drugs (e.g., peppermint, eucalyptus).
Select the drying mode: Auto-off recommended (stops when weight change < 1 mg per 30 s); time mode for non-standard determinations.
Grind or sieve the crude drug to 355–710 µm (40–25 mesh) for uniform sample exposure.
Spread 2–5 g of sample uniformly across the entire pan surface in a thin, even layer — do not pile in the centre.
Close the lid — the analyzer will begin heating automatically.
Monitor the real-time moisture percentage on the display.
At completion, record the final moisture content (%) displayed.
Open the lid carefully — use tongs as the pan is very hot (100–200°C).
Allow the pan to cool, then remove sample residue and clean.
Compare results against IP/BP/WHO limits for the specific drug.
Record: sample name, sample weight, temperature, time, and final moisture % in the logbook.
precautions: The sample pan and shield are extremely hot during and immediately after analysis — use forceps.
Spread sample uniformly — mounded samples cause uneven drying and false low readings.
Do not use for strongly corrosive samples — they damage the heater and load cell.
Calibrate using a reference standard (e.g., calcium gluconate, sodium tartrate) as per manufacturer schedule.
Allow 5-minute cooling between successive runs for consistent temperature equilibration.
Store crude drug samples in sealed containers before analysis — moisture uptake from air falsifies pre-weigh values.
For hygroscopic drugs, work quickly — minimize the time between weighing and closing the lid.
